images.filename: Junkers Ju 87 "Stuka".jpg
images.caption: A picture of a Junkers Ju 87 on display in the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago. Germany used this plane during World War II to inflict serious damage on cities and towns. The Junkers Ju 87, or "Stuka", was a dive-bomber. Each Stuka carried sirens to terrify their targets before dropping its payload. Their wings were inverted gull wings.
images.alt: A picture of a Junkers Ju 87 on display in the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago. Germany used this plane during World War II to inflict serious damage on cities and towns. The Junkers Ju 87, or "Stuka", was a dive-bomber. Each Stuka carried sirens to terrify their targets before dropping its payload. Their wings were inverted gull wings.

images.filename: Rotating Sand, Museum of Science and Industry, Jackson Park, Lake Shore Drive and 57th Street, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL (54212691466).jpg
images.caption: Opened in 1933-1940, the Griffin Museum of Science and Industry houses a collection of artifacts focusing on technology, industry, and scientific concepts.  The museum features 75 galleries containing 2,000 exhibits, as well as an Omni IMAX domed theater.  The museum welcomes more than a million visitors annually, being among several major museums and cultural attractions that can be found along Chicago’s lakefront from Lincoln Park in the north to Jackson Park in the south, and is the last surviving significant structure from the 1893 Columbian Exposition.
images.alt: Opened in 1933-1940, the Griffin Museum of Science and Industry houses a collection of artifacts focusing on technology, industry, and scientific concepts.
